mainEntity.name: How long do dental implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper care, dental implants are designed to last a lifetime. The titanium post itself typically never needs replacing. The ceramic crown may need replacement after 15 to 20 years due to normal wear. Regular cleanings and checkups at Arvada Dental Center & Implants are essential for long-term implant health, which is why our 5-Year Assurance Warranty includes two annual maintenance visits.

mainEntity.name: Does getting a dental implant hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Implant placement is performed under local anesthesia or IV sedation, so you feel no pain during the procedure. Most patients experience mild soreness and swelling for 3 to 5 days afterward, which is easily managed with over-the-counter pain relievers. Many patients report the procedure was far more comfortable than they expected, and Dr. Bennett's Moderate IV Sedation certification means even anxious patients and complex full-arch cases stay completely comfortable throughout treatment.

mainEntity.name: Does insurance cover dental implants in Arvada, Colorado?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many dental insurance plans contribute toward the crown portion of an implant, and some plans also cover the surgical placement. At Arvada Dental Center & Implants, we verify your benefits before treatment and help you maximize your coverage. Flexible financing through Cherry, CareCredit, Proceed Finance, LendingClub, and Sunbit is available to cover any remaining out-of-pocket costs, with monthly payments starting as low as $253/month.

mainEntity.name: How long does the dental implant process take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The full implant process typically takes 4 to 8 months from placement to final crown, including the 3 to 6 month osseointegration period when the implant fuses with your jawbone. For qualifying patients, we offer same-day implants with immediate temporary restorations, so you leave the office with teeth the same day as your surgery. Dr. Bennett will outline your specific timeline at your consultation.

mainEntity.name: Am I too old for dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no upper age limit for dental implants. At Arvada Dental Center & Implants, we routinely place implants in healthy patients well into their 80s. The key factors are adequate bone density, good general health, and absence of uncontrolled systemic conditions, not age. Even if you've experienced significant bone loss, advanced techniques like bone grafting and zygomatic implants often make treatment possible. We'll evaluate your candidacy at your consultation.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I don't replace a missing tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: When a tooth is lost, the jawbone at that site begins to deteriorate from lack of stimulation, a process called bone resorption. Surrounding teeth gradually shift toward the gap, affecting your bite and increasing your risk of further tooth loss, gum disease, and even facial sagging over time. Dental implants are the only tooth replacement option that prevents bone loss, because they replace the tooth root itself and continue stimulating the jawbone just like a natural tooth.

mainEntity.name: Can dental implants fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Implant failure is uncommon, with a success rate above 95% when placed by an experienced implant dentist. Risk factors include smoking, uncontrolled diabetes, and poor oral hygiene. At Arvada Dental Center & Implants, Dr. Bennett has personally placed over 5,000 implants and thoroughly evaluates your health before placement to maximize success. Our 5-Year Assurance Warranty and Zirconia Warranty also provide added protection: if an implant fails within the first 5 years on covered cases, we cover full replacement of the implant and prosthesis.

mainEntity.name: Why does Dr. Bennett use 4 to 8 implants instead of always placing exactly four?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because four isn't always the right number. The original All-On-4 protocol was built for a specific patient profile, and over the years implant dentistry has matured well past that template. Dr. Bennett evaluates your bone density, bone volume, and bite force at consultation, and he places the number of implants your case actually warrants for long-term stability. For some patients that's 4. For others it's 6 or 8. The goal is a restoration built to last 30+ years, not one that fits a marketing slogan.

mainEntity.name: How is All-On-X different from a single dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single implant replaces one missing tooth. All-On-X replaces an entire arch (12 to 14 teeth) using just 4 to 8 implants strategically angled to maximize bone contact. For patients missing most or all of their teeth, All-On-X is dramatically faster, less invasive, and more cost-effective than placing individual implants for every missing tooth.

mainEntity.name: Can I really go home with teeth the same day as surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost always, yes. In well over 99% of cases, we attach a fixed temporary bridge to your implants the same day they're placed. You leave with a complete, functional smile, eat soft food that night, and never go through a "no teeth" phase. Your final zirconia bridge is delivered 3 to 5 months later, once your implants have fully fused with your jawbone.

mainEntity.name: How long do All-On-X dental implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The titanium implants are designed to last a lifetime, and most do. The zirconia bridge sitting on top is incredibly durable and resists chipping, staining, and wear for 15 to 20 years or more under normal conditions. With twice-yearly maintenance and the protection of our 5-Year Assurance and Zirconia Warranty, your investment is protected for the long haul.

mainEntity.name: Does dental insurance cover All-On-X in Arvada, Colorado?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your plan, but more often than people realize, yes, partially. Many dental insurance policies contribute toward the surgical phase, the prosthetic phase, or both. We verify your benefits before you commit to treatment and structure the case to capture every dollar your plan will pay. Whatever insurance doesn't cover, our financing partners almost always can.

mainEntity.name: Am I too old for All-On-X?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no upper age limit on All-On-X, and we routinely place implants for patients in their 70s and 80s. The deciding factors are general health and adequate bone, not age. Patients with significant bone loss who've been turned away elsewhere often qualify with us thanks to Dr. Bennett's training in zygomatic and pterygoid implants for the most complex cases.

mainEntity.name: Is All-On-X actually better than dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: By every meaningful measure, yes. Dentures sit on your gums and shift, accelerate the bone loss that causes facial collapse over time, restore only 10 to 20% of natural chewing force, and require adhesive, soaking, and constant adjustment. All-On-X is fixed to your jaw, preserves the underlying bone, restores roughly 90% of your natural bite force, and is cared for like real teeth. The upfront cost is higher, the long-term value isn't close.

mainEntity.name: How do I clean and care for All-On-X implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost exactly like natural teeth, with one small addition. Brush twice a day, use a water flosser or interdental brush to clean underneath the bridge where dental floss won't reach, and come in for a professional cleaning every six months. That's the entire maintenance routine.

mainEntity.name: How are implant supported dentures different from traditional dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Traditional dentures rest on your gums and rely on suction or adhesive to stay in place, which is why they shift, click, and slip. Implant supported dentures snap directly onto 2 to 4 dental implants anchored in your jawbone. The result is dramatically better stability, stronger bite force, less daily frustration, and active preservation of the jawbone (which conventional dentures cannot do).

mainEntity.name: Can implant supported dentures be removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. That's actually one of their key advantages over a fixed restoration. You snap the denture into place in the morning, wear it confidently all day, and remove it at night for thorough cleaning. The implants stay in place permanently, but the denture itself is removable for easy hygiene.

mainEntity.name: How many implants do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most cases use 2 to 4 implants per arch, depending on the type of denture and your bone structure. Lower arches often work well with 2 implants. Upper arches typically need 4 for adequate stability. Dr. Bennett confirms the exact number after reviewing your 3D scan at consultation.

mainEntity.name: Do I need bone grafting for implant supported dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Patients with adequate bone density can usually go straight to implant placement. Those with moderate bone loss may need a small bone graft first, which we perform in-house. Your 3D CBCT scan gives us a clear picture of your bone volume at consultation, so you'll know exactly what's required before any treatment begins.

mainEntity.name: How is a zirconia fixed bridge different from All-On-X?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are two different things that often get confused. All-On-X describes the surgical technique (how many implants are placed and where), while a zirconia fixed bridge describes the material and type of the final prosthetic that sits on those implants. The two work together: a typical All-On-X case at our office uses 4 to 6 implants to support a zirconia bridge. The zirconia is what makes the final restoration so durable, lifelike, and long-lasting.

mainEntity.name: How long does a zirconia fixed bridge last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper care and regular checkups, a zirconia fixed bridge is designed to last 20 years or more. The titanium implants themselves are typically a lifetime solution. The zirconia bridge is highly resistant to chipping, staining, and wear, and our in-house Zirconia Warranty covers exact duplicate replacement on covered fractures within the warranty period.

mainEntity.name: Is the zirconia fixed bridge procedure painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The procedure is performed under IV sedation or local anesthesia, so you feel no pain during surgery. Most patients are genuinely surprised by how comfortable the experience is. Mild soreness and swelling for 3 to 5 days afterward is normal and easily managed with over-the-counter pain relievers or the prescription support we provide.

mainEntity.name: Is zirconia better than an acrylic hybrid bridge?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most patients, yes, significantly. Zirconia is far stronger, virtually unstainable, more lifelike in appearance, and built to last 20+ years. The long-term value is meaningfully better for patients who plan to keep their restoration for decades.

mainEntity.name: Am I really a candidate for zygomatic implants if I was told I have "no bone"?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost certainly, yes. Zygomatic implants were specifically designed for patients with severe upper jaw bone loss who cannot receive traditional implants. The technique bypasses the missing jawbone and anchors into your cheekbone instead. If you've been turned away from implants because of bone loss, denture wear, failed grafts, or sinus issues, zygomatic implants are often the exact solution you've been told doesn't exist for you.

mainEntity.name: Is the zygomatic implant procedure safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in trained hands. Zygomatic implants have been performed worldwide for over 30 years and have an exceptional safety record when placed by an experienced clinician using modern 3D planning and fully-guided surgery. Dr. Bennett has dedicated advanced training in this technique, uses cone beam CT imaging and 3D-printed surgical guides on every case, and performs the procedure under IV sedation in our Arvada office without the need for hospitalization.

mainEntity.name: Do I really get fixed teeth the same day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In almost all cases, a fixed temporary bridge is attached to your zygomatic implants the same day they are placed. You leave the office with a complete, functional smile, you eat soft food that night, and you never go through a "no teeth" phase. Your permanent zirconia bridge is delivered 3 to 4 months later once the implants have fully integrated.

mainEntity.name: How long is recovery from zygomatic implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients are comfortable enough to return to normal daily activities within 5 to 7 days after surgery, with mild cheek swelling resolving over the same window. A soft-food diet is required for the first 2 to 3 weeks while your tissues heal. Full integration of the implants takes 3 to 4 months, but you have functional fixed teeth the entire time thanks to the same-day temporary bridge.

mainEntity.name: How long do zygomatic implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zygomatic implants are designed to last a lifetime, and the zygoma (your cheekbone) is one of the densest bones in the face, which gives the implants exceptional long-term stability once integrated. The final zirconia bridge sitting on top is built to last 20 years or more. With twice-yearly maintenance and our 5-Year Assurance Warranty, your investment is protected for the long haul.

mainEntity.name: How are zygomatic implants different from All-On-X?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both create a full-arch fixed restoration, but they solve different problems. All-On-X uses 4 to 8 standard implants anchored in the jawbone, which works well for patients with adequate bone. Zygomatic implants anchor into the cheekbone instead of the jaw, which is specifically what makes them viable for patients with severe bone loss. In practice, most zygomatic cases combine both: 2 to 4 zygomatic implants for the back of the arch, plus 2 standard implants in the front where bone is typically preserved.

Age is not a barrier, and we have placed successful implants for patients in their 80s and beyond. The only way to know for certain is a consultation and 3D scan.

mainEntity.name: Does insurance cover dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coverage varies by plan. Most dental insurance plans classify implants as cosmetic and offer limited direct coverage for the implant itself, but many plans do contribute toward tooth extractions, bone grafting, the final crown, and routine cleanings during your treatment journey. We submit insurance claims electronically on your behalf, verify benefits before treatment, and help you maximize coverage. Most patients pair partial insurance with our 12+ financing partners to make the total cost manageable. You will never be surprised by unexpected bills.

mainEntity.name: Can I get teeth the same day as my implant surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most full-arch cases, yes. With same-day implants, also called teeth-in-a-day or immediate-load implants, Dr. Bennett places your implants and attaches a temporary fixed bridge in a single appointment, so you leave with a complete, functional smile. The temporary is worn during the 3 to 5 month healing period while the implants fuse with your jawbone. Your final zirconia restoration is then fabricated in our in-house dental lab and placed once integration is complete. About 99.9% of full-arch patients qualify for same-day teeth at Arvada Dental Center & Implants.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between All-On-4, All-On-X, and zygomatic implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: All-On-4 uses 4 implants per arch to support a fixed bridge. All-On-X is a broader term covering full-arch restorations using 4 to 8 implants, with the number customized to your bone quality and bite forces. Dr. Bennett often places 5 or 6 implants for upper-arch cases or patients who want maximum long-term durability, with no extra charge for additional implants. Zygomatic implants are reserved for patients with severe upper-jaw bone loss who cannot receive traditional implants, and they anchor in the cheekbone rather than the jaw, bypassing missing bone entirely and avoiding years of bone grafting.

mainEntity.name: How long does the full dental implant process take?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a single tooth implant, the full process typically takes 4 to 8 months from placement to final crown, including the 3 to 6 month osseointegration period when the implant fuses with your jawbone. For full-arch All-On-X, you leave your surgery day with a complete temporary bridge, and the final zirconia restoration is placed approximately 3 to 5 months later. The process is faster than most patients expect because you never have to go without teeth at any point during treatment.

mainEntity.name: What if I am afraid of the dentist or have dental anxiety?

acceptedAnswer.text: You are in the right place. Dental anxiety affects nearly 60% of adults, and it is one of the most common reasons patients delay implant treatment for years. At Arvada Dental Center & Implants, we offer 4 levels of sedation, from local anesthesia to nitrous oxide, oral sedation, and IV sedation, all customized to your comfort level. Dr. Bennett is Moderate IV Sedation Certified and our team monitors your vital signs continuously throughout sedation. IV sedation is included in All-On-X, Zirconia Fixed Bridge, and Zygomatic implant treatment. Most patients describe the experience as going to sleep and waking up with new teeth.

mainEntity.name: What makes Arvada Dental Center & Implants different from other implant practices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three things set us apart. First, experience. Dr. Gregory Bennett has placed over 5,000 dental implants in 24+ years and is recognized as a Top Dentist by 5280 Magazine. He performs zygomatic, pterygoid, and trans-sinus techniques that very few dentists in the country offer. Second, in-house everything. We handle every stage under one roof, including 3D CBCT imaging, surgery, IV sedation, and final restoration fabrication in our on-site dental lab. No outside referrals, no waiting on outside labs, no surprise costs. Third, pricing transparency. Our prices include the implants, IV sedation, temporary bridge, and final zirconia restoration. We do not charge extra for placing 5, 6, 7, or 8 implants instead of 4. Your case is backed by our 5-Year Assurance Warranty and extended Zirconia Warranty.

mainEntity.name: How much does a single dental implant cost in Arvada, Colorado?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single dental implant in Arvada starts at $3,795, which covers the implant, abutment, and custom crown. The final price depends on whether you need a tooth extraction or bone graft beforehand, and you get a fully itemized quote at your consultation with no figures that change later. Monthly financing is available through CareCredit, Cherry, Sunbit, PatientFi, Proceed Finance, and LendingPoint.

mainEntity.name: Is a dental implant better than a bridge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for most patients a single implant is the better long-term choice. A dental bridge requires grinding down the two healthy teeth on either side of the gap, and it does nothing to stop the bone loss underneath. An implant stands on its own, leaves your neighboring teeth untouched, and stimulates the jawbone like a natural root, which is why it typically outlasts a bridge by decades.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to get a single dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The implant placement itself usually takes under an hour. The full timeline runs about three to six months, because your jawbone needs time to fuse to the titanium post before the final crown is attached. If the missing tooth is in a visible spot, you wear a temporary the whole time, so you are never left with a gap.

mainEntity.name: Does getting a dental implant hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, most patients feel little to no pain during a single implant procedure. It is done with local anesthetic, or IV sedation if you prefer, and any soreness afterward is usually mild, lasts a day or two, and is easily managed with over-the-counter medication.

mainEntity.name: How long do dental implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single dental implant is designed to last a lifetime. The titanium post fuses permanently to your jaw, and the crown on top holds up for 15 years or more under normal conditions before it ever needs replacing, which can be done without disturbing the implant beneath it.

mainEntity.name: Does dental insurance cover dental implants in Colorado?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many dental insurance plans cover part of a single implant, often the crown or a portion of the procedure. Coverage varies by plan, so we verify your benefits before you commit and structure the treatment to capture every dollar your policy allows. Anything insurance does not cover can usually be spread into low monthly payments through our financing partners.

mainEntity.name: What is the success rate of dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental implants have one of the highest success rates in all of dentistry, up to 99% in healthy patients. At Arvada Dental Center & Implants, Dr. Bennett has personally placed over 5,000 implants, and every case is planned in advance with a 3D cone beam scan for added precision.

mainEntity.name: What if I have been told I do not have enough bone for an implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: You may still qualify. Not having enough bone is one of the most common reasons patients are turned away elsewhere, and it is often solved with a bone graft before placement. A 3D scan at your Arvada consultation shows exactly how much bone you have and what your case needs.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with a dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, once your implant has healed you can eat virtually anything you want. Because the implant is anchored in your jaw rather than resting on the gums, it restores nearly the full bite force of a natural tooth, so foods like steak, apples, and nuts are back on the menu.

mainEntity.name: How do I take care of a single dental implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: You care for an implant exactly like a natural tooth. Brush twice a day, floss around it, and keep your six-month cleanings at our Arvada office. There is nothing to remove, soak, or adjust.
